newsitem.title: USA: U.S. see "struggles for power" in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. see "struggles for power" in Iraq.

text.p: The White House said on Wednesday it sees internal "struggles for power" going on in Iraq for control.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry, asked for his assessment of reports by a senior U.S. military official that Iraqi President Saddam Hussein has put his wife under house arrest, said: "There are a great deal of complicated internal struggles for power" going on.

A senior U.S. military official at the Pentagon on Tuesday gave no details on when or why Saddam's wife might have been restricted but suggested a shooting attack on Saddam's son, Uday, last month might have prompted the president's increased fear for his own safety. He said the son may lose a leg to gangrene.
"There have been some things that have happened there recently ... that have been reported publicly that would indicate some internal machinations," McCurry said.
McCurry said the United States was "closely monitoring" the situation in Iraq.

"The president also has foremost on his mind the threats to regional security, particularly in the Persian Gulf," McCurry said, adding that there were no indications of troop movements that would suggest any renewed threat to Kuwait.
